events.excerpt: This post follows Informed Diffusion: making home builders publish fast (2026). Author: @cskiraly Update, 29 October 2026: this post stays as published. Its text is kept current, with the latest results, on notes.ethereum.org , and each version, with its data and scripts, at eth-networking-studies . SEACAST’s specification and its releases are at informed-diffusion-spec ; news is posted as replies to this topic. TL;DR Ethereum has more and more large objects to broadcast, and little time for each. Today’s payloads are small and datacenters carry them, which is much of why mainnet is in time, but payloads grow (with gas increase and block-level access lists, BALs) and timelines shrink (with quick slots). Execution proofs and consensus blocks with post-quantum signatures may soon join the large-message club too. Today’s delivery method (gossipsub) sits far from being optimal : every node waits for the whole object before passing it on, and receives several copies of it. From a builder at home, the last nodes receive a 1 MiB payload seconds late. Not every node needs every byte. With data-availability sampling, a node is to receive its samples of an object, not the object. PeerDAS’s 128 column topics are only one way of doing sampled diffusion; RowDAS and FullDAS are other examples.
events.headline: SEACAST: fast, lean, sampled broadcast for Ethereum, with an executable spec and a formal model

events.excerpt: Today, we are expanding our web application firewall (WAF) by adding two new capabilities: full transaction detections and response rules. Full transaction detections evaluate each HTTP request alongside its response to identify evidence of exploitation. It helps answer both "Does this request look malicious?" and "What happened when the application handled it?" Response rules can then block the origin’s response before it reaches the requester. These are valuable protections because the latest frontier models are uncovering vulnerabilities buried deep in widely used software, giving defenders clarity on what to fix — and attackers new paths to exploit. The recent php2shell vulnerability shows the stakes: a flaw in a common software component can put applications across the Internet at risk. AI agents scanning for vulnerabilities can be extremely persistent, adapting payloads using feedback, and chaining vulnerabilities, credentials, and permissions. An application's response can reveal whether an attempt worked and give an attacker information that helps them go deeper. Inspecting incoming requests remains essential for stopping recognizable attacks before they reach an application. But some threats become clear only when the request is considered alongside what the origin retur
events.headline: Introducing full transaction detection for Cloudflare WAF

All Cloudflare WAF customers are protected against known exploit attempts if their site uses PHP's default upload progress field name. Customers who have changed session.upload_progress.name are not covered by the WAF rule. The existing rules "PHP Remote Code Execution Attack (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) #6" protects against this vulnerability. More information to follow. October 21, Calif.io, Wiz, OpenAI and Quarkslab disclosed two vulnerabilities in PHP, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 and known as php2shell . Cloudflare has been part of a coordinated effort to deploy mitigations to protect the Internet, working with PHP foundation , OpenAI and Wiz among others. events.excerpt: Opening community discussion on URC-5: Token Venue Policy . Some tokens recommend particular liquidity pools or restrict trading to supported venues, often because their mechanics depend on a Uniswap v4 hook (INDEX, STANDARD, FWA, etc). Without a shared way to discover those policies, routers and frontends need token-specific integrations and may otherwise offer unsupported routes. Anecdotally, STANDARD and FWA prevented a lot of trading volume due to routers routing to restricted pools and required bespoke integrations for both. URC-5 defines IVenuePolicy , a token-level interface for declaring canonical v4 pools, distinguishing Preferred and Enforced policies, and exposing directional permissions for other liquidity venues. It also specifies how routers, aggregators, and frontends should interpret those declarations. Transfer-time enforcement remains token-specific. We’d appreciate input from hook developers, token teams, routers, aggregators, and frontend implementers. 6 posts - 4 participants Read full topic
events.headline: URC-5: Token Venue Policy

events.excerpt: AI can write code and pass the bar exam, but it still struggles to buy a pair of shoes online. That’s because websites were built for humans, not agents. Most agents that shop for someone today work from a site’s HTML — they look at the page, guess which button does what, click, and try again when they get it wrong. This process is slow, uses a lot of tokens, and something as seemingly innocuous as a theme change can break it. Enter WebMCP: a browser standard from Google that gives AI agents structured tools on a page, like search_products . Instead of hunting for buttons, the agent calls the exact tool it needs directly, making shopping faster, cheaper, and far more reliable. Because WebMCP is still an experimental proposed browser standard in early preview, it’s currently available behind experimental Chrome flags ( chrome://flags/#enable-webmcp-testing ), in Chrome Origin Trials, in some agentic browsers, and across developer environments like Cloudflare Kitesurf . In August, we launched edge implementation of WebMCP in beta. Turn it on, and Cloudflare injects a tiny script at the edge to make those tools available automatically, without site owners writing a single line of code. events.excerpt: On October 19, 2026, at approximately 17:00 UTC, Cloudflare became aware that private keys associated with eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were compromised. These certificates were widely trusted by browsers, operating systems, and also within Cloudflare. Because the keys themselves are weak, an attacker can create a forged certificate for any domain and use it to impersonate servers to intercept or modify traffic. This is a serious security incident with implications across the Internet. For reference, here is a link to more information about how SSL certificates work and why they are so critical to the operation of the Internet. We immediately prioritized patching critical services across Cloudflare to protect our customers ahead of the public disclosure of the vulnerability. Our security review has not identified active exploitation of this issue on Cloudflare services. We have released updates for the Cloudflare One Clients, also known as WARP or the 1.1.1.1 app, and Cloudflare Tunnel, also known as cloudflared. We have also deployed mitigations across our CDN, Developer, and Zero Trust products. As those original members were arrested or jailed one by one, control over the ShinyHunters brand eventually passed to “ Rey ,” identified last year as a teenage hacker from Amman, Jordan. events.excerpt: In collaboration with @winderica TLDR: we port Tornado Cash to Flock, a post-quantum binary-field SNARK, proving a depth-32 withdrawal over SHA-256 in under 30 ms, and describe a simple recovery protocol, requiring only that wallets derive note secrets from a seed, that lets existing pools survive a discrete log break. Introduction Privacy pools such as Tornado Cash rest on the hardness of the discrete logarithm, through both their Pedersen commitments and their Groth16 proofs. Recent autoresearch efforts, both at lowering quantum resource estimates and at breaking hash functions , suggest that quantum discrete-logarithm circuits with far lower gate counts than the published ones, and yet-undiscovered attacks on the hash functions these pools use, may already exist. Recent progress in binary-field proving systems, ZCash’s deployment of ZIP 2005 in Ironwood, and the leanVM aggregation work all point the same way: privacy pools should now start to transition their stack to battle-tested cryptographic primitives. In this post we demonstrate a working Tornado Cash-like pool built on Flock : a plausibly post-quantum transparent hash based binary-field SNARK. We instantiate its merkle tree and nullifier derivation function with SHA-256. We also describe a simple quantum recoverability

events.excerpt: Hey Cosmonauts, I’ve been exploring an idea for a privacy-focused Cosmos SDK chain and wanted to bring it here before going too far into implementation. The idea is called VeilRoute — a sovereign Cosmos blockchain that acts as a confidential settlement and asset-routing layer between IBC-connected chains. The problem I’m interested in is relatively simple: Cosmos has interoperability through IBC, but what if applications could route assets through a common privacy layer without publicly exposing every internal transfer, amount, balance, or ownership relationship? I’m not proposing changes to the Cosmos Hub or requesting governance funding. This is an early architectural discussion to get technical feedback from people working on Cosmos SDK, IBC, ZK systems, and interchain security. 1. The idea Imagine a user moving ATOM from Cosmos Hub to Osmosis. Today, the public source and destination transactions are observable, along with the relevant IBC packet information. With VeilRoute, the proposed flow would be: Cosmos Hub / Other IBC Chain | IBC Deposit | v +---------------+ | VeilRoute | | | | Shielded Pool | | ZK Validation | | Private Notes | | Audit Records | +---------------+ | IBC Withdrawal | v Destination IBC Chain Users would deposit an IBC asset, shield it into a private not

events.excerpt: Should the Cosmos Hub have its own price oracle? CosmWasm is now permissionless on the Hub, but there is no price oracle available to contracts. Pyth dropped CosmWasm, SEDA is EVM-only, and Band over IBC is slow and costs fees on every query. Without prices, we can’t build any advanced defi on the Hub. So these apps get built on chains like Injective or dYdX, and ATOM ends up used everywhere except on its own chain. Idea: integrate an enshrined oracle based on the Slinky fork. Validators would publish prices at every block, secured by the Hub’s own validator set, with no dependency on an external provider. And beyond the Hub: these prices could be distributed over IBC to any connected chain that lacks an oracle. The Hub would become an interchain’s price provider, with fees flowing back to ATOM stakers. Longer term: prices are only the first step. The same validator-voted mechanism could later carry other data the interchain needs, such as LST exchange rates, proof of reserves or other verified off-chain data. The Hub would become the interchain’s trusted data layer. The Community Pool could fund the development and audit. Would you support this direction? Validators, would you be willing to run an oracle sidecar? 20 posts - 7 participants Read full topic

events.excerpt: v2.10.3 is a security and stability release on top of v2.10.2 . It's the public release of v2.10.3-priv , which most validators and major RPC providers already run. No hardfork, no database schema change, no resync required. Nodes can be upgraded one at a time, in any order. Highlights Execution : parallel (BlockSTM V2) balance reads are resolved correctly across a self-destruct boundary ( #2403 ). Shared block caches are size-capped and per-tx code hashes memoized, which lowers importer memory under heavy keccak / ecrecover load. Log counting while tracing no longer copies logs ( #2460 ). Txpool : pending chains stranded behind a head that can't be mined are evicted after txpool.strandedlifetime . Filtered addresses also apply to SetCode (type 4) authorizations. The pool signer is no longer swapped when allow-unprotected-txs is set ( #2464 ). Storage trie preload : segmented BFS queue for the preload, plus optional address-cache persistence across restarts. On a mainnet sentry, preload on restart drops from about 1h25m to about 4s. P2P : static peers stay dialed across jails and full dynamic slots ( #2438 ), and are kept out of the peer dropper. RPC : the execution slot is re-acquired between batch items, and the RPC execution pool request timeout from config is applied. Heimdal

events.excerpt: The United Kingdom has issued economic sanctions against Cryptomus , a chameleonic cryptocurrency platform that experts say serves as a major conduit for payments related to ransomware, narcotics, darknet markets, fraud and cybercrime services that are helping Russia circumvent existing financial restrictions. Heleket’s support agent on Telegram claims, despite all evidence to the contrary, that it is not affiliated with Cryptomus. Image: Richard Sanders. On October 8, the U.K. issued sanctions (PDF) against Cryptomus — previously known as Certa Payments and Xeltox Enterprises — for processing payments that benefit the Russian government and its financial institutions. The sanctions freeze any Cryptomus assets at U.K. banks, and bar British companies from offering it any business, virtual or otherwise. Also targeted in these sanctions were the virtual payment platforms VexPay , TokenSpot , and the Tsunami Payments service . As explained in our December 2024 investigation, “ How Cryptocurrency Turns to Cash in Russian Banks ,” Cryptomus has been a key payment processor for dozens of Russian cryptocurrency exchanges and websites hawking cybercrime services.
